clue.text: Seashore observed in view across river

indicators.note: across means the word for view stretches over the river's letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a stand is a position or point of view, as in taking a stand

explanation.surface: Someone notices a coastline seen from the far bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed in' is linking: the definition is seen in what follows. 'across' puts STAND around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a literary word for a beach or shore.

clue.text: Suppose president will need summary

parts.note: a resumé is a summary, of a career for instance

explanation.surface: Guessing that a head of state will want a briefing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to take something for granted, i.e. assume or suppose it.

clue.text: Laugh at girl's anger when dad comes in

indicators.note: comes in tells us the word for dad enters between the other pieces

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, with the possessive S giving DIS
rage is fierce anger
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A girl's temper is mocked whenever her father walks into the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage is to belittle or scorn, a close sense of mocking someone.

clue.text: Fairies getting hot die

parts.note: peris are fairy-like beings of Persian mythology
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Fairies feel the heat and expire.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to lose one's life, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Alexander swallows hot drink

indicators.note: swallows means the name takes the abbreviation for hot inside it

parts.note: Sandy is a familiar short form of Alexander
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man called Alexander gulps down a hot beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander is not a person to define but a name to shorten: SANDY.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a beverage of beer mixed with lemonade, popular in Britain.

clue.text: Part of body not sleek sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A body part regrettably lacks smoothness.
explanation.definitionFit: The bony framework is a structure within the human frame, so loosely one part of it.

clue.text: A Conservative man appeared on stage maybe

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
Ted is a typical man's name in crosswords

explanation.surface: A Tory politician turned up in a theatre, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To have performed a role in a play is to have appeared on stage; 'maybe' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Person giving testimony opened unusual new testament

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of opened are rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: A witness opens an odd new version of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A deponent is a legal term for someone making a sworn statement as a witness.

clue.text: Insects and arachnids appearing after second half of winter

indicators.note: appearing after places the arachnid word behind the piece from winter
second half of tells us to take only the latter three letters of winter

parts.note: mites are tiny arachnids, relatives of spiders

explanation.surface: Bugs and spiders emerging as winter draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are wood-eating social bugs that build mounds.

clue.text: Bureaucracy evident with something bound to look colourful?

explanation.surface: Officialdom is obvious, tied up in bright ribbons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evident with' links the two readings; the second describes literally tape that is red, bound round documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive official rules are called this after the coloured ribbon once tying government papers; that literal ribbon is the second sense.

clue.text: Famous Greek from Thermopylae, so powerful

indicators.note: from signals that the name is drawn out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A celebrated Greek hailing from the mighty pass of Thermopylae.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was an ancient Greek storyteller known for his fables.

clue.text: Afterthought about a county town expanding

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: PS (postscript) is an afterthought added to a letter
Reading is the county town of Berkshire, England

explanation.surface: A footnote concerning a provincial town that is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses PS to SP. READING is the county town of Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading means extending or stretching out over a wider area.

clue.text: Fruit not right — it's a vegetable

indicators.note: not tells us the abbreviation for right is missing from the fruit

parts.note: a pear is a common orchard fruit

explanation.surface: This produce is not quite a fruit; it belongs among the greens.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a small green seed eaten as a garden vegetable.

clue.text: Walk into river to make a diplomatic gesture

indicators.note: into shows the walking word going inside the river name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to march is to walk in a determined step

explanation.surface: Wading into a river as a political statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A démarche is a formal step or representation made through diplomatic channels.

clue.text: Port provided by big nurse

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for large
to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: A harbour supplied by a large hospital carer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian ferry harbour on the North Sea.

clue.text: Sauce gran poured out? There's something sweet in it

indicators.note: poured out suggests the letters spill and settle in a different order

explanation.surface: Granny's sauce spilled out, and it contains something sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall grass is a plant whose stems hold sucrose, the source of much table sugar.

clue.text: Vandal could wreck boat, sure!

indicators.note: could wreck signals that the letters are smashed and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A hooligan really might sink the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages property, much like a vandal.

clue.text: Booze may be something that ensnares

explanation.surface: Alcohol can be a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits flavoured with juniper are one drink; a snare or trap for game is the second sense.

clue.text: It's swell, being safely home after run?

explanation.surface: Making it back safely after a sprint is great.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who reaches the CREASE after running is safely in, hence IN CREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger; the cricket reading describes a batter safe within the marked line.

clue.text: Fresh-sounding beast

indicators.note: sounding means the word for fresh is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: An animal that seems young and novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu is an African antelope, also called a wildebeest.

clue.text: Sporting implement taken by number to be a piece of wood

parts.note: a bat is used in cricket or baseball
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A bat bought by a team of players becomes timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' is only linking order here, with the implement coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: A batten is a long thin strip of timber used in building.

clue.text: In America kill for diamonds

explanation.surface: Murder in the US for jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang uses the word for murdering someone; it is also slang for gems.

clue.text: Double hesitation to take on pet food supplier

indicators.note: to take on means the pet is placed in front of the hesitation sounds

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet

indicators.note: Double means the hesitation sound is written twice

parts.note: er is a hesitant sound in speech

explanation.surface: Two pauses before taking on an animal provider.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer provides meals for functions.

clue.text: Outside a scientist's workplace there's brass pipe

indicators.note: Outside means the money word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a lab is where a scientist works

explanation.surface: Beyond the lab lies a brass musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is not the metal but northern British slang for money; 'Outside' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A calabash is a gourd, and also a smoking pipe whose bowl is made from one.

clue.text: Valuable material kept by tot and cherished

indicators.note: kept by tells us the mineral is held inside the totting word

parts.note: to tot up is to add
ore is rock containing metal worth extracting

explanation.surface: A precious item held by a toddler and loved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child; here it is the verb, to tot up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply, so close to cherished.

clue.text: Good little house, a cosy den?

parts.note: ho is a short form of house
a nest is a snug den or retreat

explanation.surface: A small dwelling makes a pleasant snug retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest means upright and truthful, one sense of good.

clue.text: Agreed to study dog showing evidence of high temperature?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a cur is a mongrel dog
metal glows red when very hot, as in red-hot

explanation.surface: Agreed to examine a hound with a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurred means went along with or were of the same opinion.

clue.text: Vehicle carries a small weight of stones

indicators.note: carries means the vehicle holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: A wagon transports rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a unit of mass for gems, 200 milligrams.

clue.text: Virtuous family full of energy

indicators.note: full of shows the family word holding the energy abbreviation

parts.note: a clan is an extended family
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A pure-living family bursting with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the moral sense means pure or free of wrongdoing.

clue.text: What's potentially great as crowd controller

indicators.note: potentially means the letters could be made into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Something possibly brilliant for handling a mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use this irritant spray to disperse rioters.

clue.text: It could be shown by girl having less on the outside!

definitions.text: It could be shown by girl having less on the outside!

indicators.note: on the outside means the word less is wrapped round the name

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wearing skimpy clothing might show how thin she is.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a girl wearing less clothing shows how thin she is.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thin or slender means lacking fat, which is what scanty clothing reveals.

clue.text: Court order gets the man to squirm

parts.note: a writ is a written order from a court
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A legal summons makes a man wriggle.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, as in pain.
